record.what_it_does: Corporate card, spend management, bill pay and accounting automation platform for businesses.
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 with two grants. Client Credentials is for your own business. Authorization Code is for third-party apps that other businesses authorize; refresh tokens must be enabled per app. Access tokens last 1 hour (authorization code) or 10 days (client credentials). A multi-user toolkit would use Authorization Code. Apps that access a whole business need an Admin or Business Owner to approve.
record.access_notes: Client IDs come from the Ramp Developer Console, which needs a Ramp account. The sandbox has no self-serve signup on the page I read; it points to a "Get Sandbox Access" request page, which I could not read. I found no documented review process for public distribution. The docs mention apps listed on ramp.com/integrations, and partner-only scopes sit in a partner console. I could not confirm whether the API needs a paid plan, so this verdict is a best guess.
record.api_breadth_notes: Developer API v1 covers transactions, cards, users, departments, bills, vendors, reimbursements, spend programs and more. The generated mcparmory-ramp package exposes 186 tools, which suggests the API is broad. I did not count operations from Ramp's own spec.
record.mcp_notes: Hosted at https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp (Ramp MCP). Sign-in acts as the signed-in user with Full or Read-only access, and connections expire after 30 days. A custom client needs its redirect URI allowlisted by Ramp. There is also a Ramp Data MCP that needs a Ramp Data API key. Ramp also publishes a local ramp-public/ramp_mcp package that runs against demo or prod using client credentials. The older Developer MCP has been retired.
record.blocker_notes: Sandbox access appears to be requested rather than instant. Third-party OAuth apps are approved per customer by an Admin. Public distribution may involve Ramp approval or partner status, but I couldn't confirm either. Real use needs a Ramp customer account.

evidence.quote: Ramp uses OAuth 2.0. Your app gets tokens from /developer/v1/token.
Demo accounts cannot process actual financial transactions
Webhooks allow your application to receive real-time notifications about events that occur in your Ramp account.

record.needs_human: Check four things. (1) The Get Sandbox Access page, for who qualifies. (2) Whether public Authorization Code apps need Ramp approval or partner status. (3) Whether the API needs a paid Ramp plan. (4) The webhook and OpenAPI details. I only saw them listed in the docs index and the shell page, and I didn't open the spec.
